default_port_notes.9000: PRIMARY — HTTP REST API + Web Console + ILP over HTTP. Attack surface: SQL exec, CSV import/export, admin-equivalent web console.
default_port_notes.9009: InfluxDB Line Protocol (ILP) over TCP — write-only ingest path.
default_port_notes.8812: PostgreSQL wire protocol — real Postgres startup handshake, connects with psql/any pg client.
default_port_notes.9003: Min health-check/metrics server — unauthenticated by design, low value but confirms liveness + version banner.

auth_default: SPLIT POSTURE by protocol. HTTP (9000, REST+console+ILP/HTTP): auth OFF by default — http.user/http.password both default unset ('N/A'), no credentials exist to guess or disable. PGWire (8812): auth is ALWAYS ON but ships a HARDCODED DEFAULT CREDENTIAL PAIR pg.user=admin / pg.password=quest — a known-default-creds exploitation class, not a true auth-bypass. http.security.readonly and pg.security.readonly both default false, so unauthenticated/default-cred sessions get INSERT/CREATE TABLE, not just SELECT.
auth_config_env: pg.readonly.user / pg.readonly.password — default 'user' / 'quest', only active if pg.readonly.user.enabled=true (default false)
QDB_PG_USER / QDB_PG_PASSWORD — Docker env equivalents, _FILE suffix variants supported
default_creds: HTTP: none configured by default — auth fully disabled, no creds exist
PGWire: admin / quest (hardcoded default, live unless operator overrides pg.user/pg.password)
PGWire readonly: user / quest (only active if pg.readonly.user.enabled=true, default false)
install_tell: Web console at '/' is a React SPA (@questdb/web-console npm package) — distinctive JS bundle name/path. Port 9003 min health server returns a QuestDB-shaped response with zero auth even when 9000 is filtered.
misconfig_patterns: 9000 exposed with http.user/http.password unset -> full unauth SQL exec + CSV import/export + admin-equivalent web console
8812 exposed with pg.user/pg.password never changed from admin/quest -> default-cred PGWire login, same blast radius via a Postgres client instead of REST
http.security.readonly=false (default) paired with open HTTP -> unauth writes (CREATE TABLE, INSERT, DROP), not just reads
ILP over HTTP/TCP (9009) frequently left open for high-throughput ingest with no auth layer in OSS builds — write-only pivot even if 9000 is otherwise locked down

Reverse-proxy-only auth (nginx basic auth in front of 9000, per QuestDB's own 2022 blog on this exact gap) — if the proxy is misrouted or bypassed via direct :9000 access, the backend has zero auth of its own

passive: Web console root ('/') returns QuestDB-branded HTML/JS bundle referencing @questdb/web-console
PGWire handshake on 8812 reports a QuestDB server_version string in the Postgres startup response

response_markers: JSON envelope: {"query":..., "columns":[...], "dataset":[...], "count":...} — QuestDB-specific column/dataset shape distinguishes from InfluxDB/TimescaleDB JSON
active_probe.false_positive_check: SELECT 1 trivial query confirms the dataset/columns envelope shape before treating as positive.

engine_routing.shodan_visible: Candidate dorks unverified against live Shodan web UI this pass — doc-grounded research only, route to Step 0 harvest for validation.

deployment_tells: Official Docker image exposes 9000/9009/8812/9003 identically per questdb.com/docs/deployment/docker/ — the 4-port cluster itself is a tell
Cloud marketplace listings (DigitalOcean, AWS) reference the same default port set and http.user/pg.user config surface
QuestDB Enterprise (separate product) adds RBAC/OIDC/LDAP — presence of those auth layers indicates Enterprise, not OSS
pivot_paths: /exec -> arbitrary SQL execution: table enumeration, schema dump, data read of any table
/exp -> bulk CSV export of query results = direct exfil primitive, no /exec JSON parsing needed
/imp -> CSV upload = write primitive; can create/overwrite tables server-side
PGWire admin/quest login -> same SQL surface via any Postgres client/driver, useful when HTTP is proxied/WAF'd but 8812 is reachable directly
ILP write path (9009) -> blind data injection into existing/new tables even without read access — data-poisoning framing
QuestDB SQL COPY and file-system functions in some configs may expose filesystem read/write beyond table data — unconfirmed, verification-stage question
vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-0824 / GHSA-xf94-h87h-g9wr: XSS in @questdb/web-console (QuestDB UI), affected up to 1.11.9, fixed 1.1.10 (QuestDB 9.3.0). CVSS 3.5 LOW. Requires user interaction (victim opens malicious link) — not a direct unauth data-exposure vector, but chains against an admin with the web console open on an otherwise-open instance.

No published GitHub Security Advisories for questdb/questdb as of this pass — no unauth-RCE CVE specific to QuestDB core found. Primary risk class is misconfiguration (auth-off-by-default HTTP + static PGWire default creds), not a code-level CVE.
auth_default_thesis: CONFIRMED, split by protocol. HTTP (9000) ships fully unauthenticated out of the box — no default creds exist to disable. PGWire (8812) ships authenticated-but-static (admin/quest hardcoded default). An exposed OSS QuestDB instance is compromised either via true auth-bypass on 9000 or known-default-credential login on 8812, both converging on the same SQL/data surface. This two-surface split changes both verification-stage probe design and dork strategy — worth its own methodology note distinct from single-surface platforms in this category.
